title: 電気回路基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits
keywords: DC circuits 2.Ohm’s law 3.Kirchhoff’s law 4.Superposition principle 5.AI utilization
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn about electric circuits having resistance (R) that are connected to DC power sources. Particular emphasis will be placed on how to formulate and solve the network equations based on Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s law.
advice: Below is an outline of the topics to be covered: DC circuits: electric circuits and Ohm’s law, Kirchhoff’s law, superposition principle, Thevenin’s Theorem, Δ-Y conversion, electric power, electric power quantity Calculation This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit I, Electrical Circuit II, and Electrical Circuit III), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a special basic course requirement. Since the progress is adjusted while checking the level of student understanding indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and the course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. Therefore, we encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don’t understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can explain Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s law in DC circuits.
Participants can formulate and solve equations for DC networks.
Participants can calculate the maximum power condition in DC circuits.
Participants can calculate DC circuits using the superposition principle and Thevenin's theorem.

achievementLevels.ideal: Participants can sufficiently explain the physical and mathematical implications of Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s laws. Using their knowledge, they can correctly calculate voltages, currents, and energy in DC circuits. They can also fully explain the equilibrium conditions of a bridge circuit. They can sufficiently explain the superposition principle and Thevenin’s theorem and correctly apply them to DC circuits.
achievementLevels.standard: Participants can explain the basic physical and mathematical implications of Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s laws. Using their knowledge, they can calculate voltages, currents and energy in the DC circuits. They can also explain the equilibrium conditions of a bridge circuit. They can explain the superposition principle and Thevenin’s theorem and apply them to DC circuits.

lessons.content: Chapter 1 Circuit Elements 1.1 Basic circuit elements 1.2 Element voltage and current (for resistance R) 1.3 Element energy (for resistance R) Integrated learning: consideration of familiar electrical products and circuits.
lessons.operation: Lecture, practices, and questions. In principle, subtests are conducted as many times as is appropriate with advance notice. And the test is explained appropriately.
lessons.assignments: Read the sections of the textbook indicated in the left column. Review the matters learned that day. Write the correct answers for the tests. Be sure to submit your report by the deadline. Review the lecture and learn more about circuit elements. Study textbooks to understand Ohm's Law and series-parallel connection of resistors.

lessons.content: Chapter 2 Fundamentals of DC Circuits 2.1 Ohm's law 2.2 Series-parallel connection of resistors
lessons.assignments: Review the lecture and deepen your understanding of Ohm's law and series-parallel connection of resistors. Study textbooks to understand voltage and current sources.

lessons.content: Chapter 2 Fundamentals of DC Circuits 2.3 Voltage and current sources
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of voltage and current sources. Study textbooks and understand the power, the electric energy and the maximum power condition in DC circuits.

lessons.content: Chapter 2 Fundamentals of DC Circuits 2.4 Power and electric energy
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the power, the electric energy and the maximum power condition in DC circuits. Study textbooks to understand Kirchhoff's laws.

lessons.content: Chapter 3 DC network equation 3.1 Kirchhoff’s laws
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the Kirchhoff's laws. Study textbooks to understand how to create the network equations.

lessons.content: Chapter 3 DC network equation 3.2 How to make the network equations Kirchhoff's Law Exercise 1
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of how to create the network equations.

lessons.content: Chapter 3 DC network equation 3.3 Solving the network equations Kirchhoff’s Law Exercise 2
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of how to solve the network equations. Study textbooks to understand the bridge circuit.

lessons.content: Chapter 4 Various DC circuits 4.1 Bridge circuit
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the bridge circuit. Study textbooks to understand the superposition principle.

lessons.content: Chapter 4 Various DC circuits 4.2 Superposition principle
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the superposition principle. Study textbooks to understand Thevenin's theorem.

lessons.content: Chapter 4 Various DC circuits 4.3 Thevenin's theorem
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of Thevenin's theorem. Study textbooks to understand the Δ-Y conversion.

lessons.content: Chapter 4 Various DC circuits 4.4 Δ-Y conversion
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the lecture and deepen your understanding of the Δ-Y conversion.

lessons.operation: The exam covers the content of all lectures.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture and exercise questions that were not fully answered in the final exam.

lessons.content: Integrated learning of this course, Self-evaluation
lessons.operation: Return the final exam and explain the questions and answers. Clear unmet action goals identified in previous tests.
lessons.assignments: Self-check and try to resolve any lack of understanding of the previous practices and test questions.
